description.en: Rabbi Hananyah ben Teradyon studied Torah under Rabbi Yose ben Kisma until Rabbi Yose felt it was counterproductive. Alongside Rabbi Elazar ben Parta, they were captured by the Romans. Rabbi Hananyah predicted that Rabbi Elazar would be saved due to his extensive acts of kindness, whereas Rabbi Hananyah himself excelled primarily in Torah study. Rabbi Hananyah was the father of Bruriah, who became the wife of Rabbi Meir.
description.he: רבי חנניה בן תרדיון למד אצל רבי יוסי בן קיסמא עד שרבו הזהירו שלימוד זה עלול להיחשב מרד בשלטון הרומאי. לאחר שהרומאים תפסו אותו ואת רבי אלעזר בן פרטא, הוא חזה שרבי אלעזר יינצל בזכות עיסוקו בתורה ובגמילות חסדים, בעוד הוא עצמו עסק רק בתורה. רבי חנניה היה אביה של ברוריה, אשתו של רבי מאיר.

en.title: Fortunate in Persecution
en.prompt: Rabbi Elazar ben Perata considered Rabbi Ḥanina ben Teradyon fortunate for being arrested on only one charge, specifically for teaching Torah publicly, while he himself faced multiple charges. The Talmudic tractate Avodah Zara recounts the arrest of these rabbis during a period of Roman religious persecution.

en.title: The Holistic Approach to Torah Study
en.ai_title: The Holistic Approach to Torah Study
en.prompt: Engaging solely in Torah study without acts of kindness is insufficient, as illustrated by Rabbi Hananyah ben Teradyon's contrast with Rabbi Elazar ben Parta in Netivot Olam. This highlights the necessity of combining Torah study with acts of kindness to fulfill divine commandments and embrace God's presence fully.
en.ai_prompt: Engaging solely in Torah study without acts of kindness is insufficient and likened to having no God. The Maharal of Prague, in his 16th-century work Netivot Olam, emphasizes the necessity of combining Torah study with acts of kindness to truly fulfill the commandments and accept God's divinity.
